Dear Fellow Shareholders:
Our experience differentiates us. Atlanticus has passed the 22-year mark as a company, and we have
experienced a great deal of change during that time. Consumers, the debt markets, the economy, and the
regulatory environment have all changed in many ways. One thing that has not changed is our core
reason for operating this company:
Atlanticus exists to create value for consumers, our employees and our shareholders.
Consumers

the U.S. economy continues to perform at historic levels, not all consumers have reaped the rewards.
This is particularly true of the consumer segment we serve. 75% of U.S. adults live paycheck to

have credit scores less than 700. Regardless of the recent macroeconomic success, the need for the

and most experienced team in the industry. The best in the business. During the recession, our
employees made the decision to persevere with Atlanticus. This was not because we were having
financial success or because they did not have other opportunities. It was a very difficult and challenging
time for almost all financial firms. They stuck with us because they believe in what we are doing and
because we care about one another. This is evident in our day to day interactions and supported by the
employee surveys we conduct. One consistent comment we hear from team members is that “Atlanticus

to how we treat our customers. We do not believe that a company can have great customer satisfaction
unless it starts with outstanding employee satisfaction.

Business Update
Experience is not being old or outdated, it is about being knowledgeable and constantly evolving. Since
our founding in 1996, we have constantly evolved. Over our 22 years we have added products and
marketing channels and expanded geographically. We have contracted when necessary and
opportunistic ally entered and exited lines of business. We have faced macroeconomic downturns and
expansions and dealt with both exuberant and excessively tight liquidity markets. We have gone head to
head with competitors, new and old, both rational and irrational.
Although our assets performed as modeled during the recession (it is well documented that less than
prime consumer assets showed much less volatility than other asset classes during the recession, and our
assets were no exception), we felt it prudent to wait until we were more comfortable with both the
changing regulatory rules by which we were to operate our business and the certainty of access to
liquidity before reinvesting in growth. While we were hesitant to deploy capital in asset growth, we did
invest in maintaining the team and infrastructure needed to serve our market when we were once again
comfortable deploying capital. That time has come.

file data and our proprietary risk evaluation systems developed and refined over our 22-year operating history. These
strategies include the management of transaction authorizations, account renewals, credit line modifications and collection
programs. We use an adaptive control system to translate our strategies into account management processes. The system
enables us to develop and test multiple strategies simultaneously, which allows us to continually refine our account
management activities. We have incorporated our proprietary risk scores into the control system, in addition to standard
credit behavior scores used widely in the industry, in order to segment, evaluate and manage the receivables. We believe
that by combining external credit file data along with historical and current customer activity, we are able to better predict
the true risk associated with current and delinquent receivables.

financial products and services to consumers who may have been declined under traditional financing options.

related services. From time to time, we also purchase receivables portfolios from third parties. References to "receivables"
include receivables purchased from our lending partners and from third parties. As discussed further below, we reflect our
